evidence.claim: The organisation states on its own website that it accepts zakat and holds it in a designated zakat account.
evidence.quote: Jamuna Learning Trust accepts zakat. We hold it in a designated zakat account with our bank in Melbourne, separate from our general donations and from our DGR-restricted funds.

evidence.claim: The campaign narrative repeats that the trust accepts zakat and administers it in a designated account.
evidence.quote: Jamuna Learning Trust accepts zakat and holds it in a designated zakat account with our bank in Melbourne, separate from our general donations and from our DGR-restricted funds.

evidence.claim: The organisation states it applies a one-eighth administrative ceiling specifically to zakat received, indicating it administers zakat as zakat.
evidence.quote: We hold to a ceiling of one eighth of zakat received.

evidence.claim: The organisation states zakat is not pooled with other funds and is not spent on unrestricted costs.
evidence.quote: It is not pooled and it is not used for unrestricted costs.

evidence.claim: Households that fail the zakat screen are paid from general donations and booked separately, implying two distinct funding streams.
evidence.quote: A household failing 2.1 or answering Y to 2.2 is funded from general donations and recorded separately.

evidence.claim: Zakat is released only to households that pass a zakat-specific eligibility screen with stated nisab and duplication tests.
evidence.quote: Zakat is released only to households that pass a zakat eligibility screen applied in addition to our means test. Assets below nisab, and no zakat received from another distributing body in the same period.

evidence.claim: The enrolment pack contains a documented zakat eligibility screen applied before zakat funds are released.
evidence.quote:
Applied in addition to Part 1, before zakat funds are released to the household.
2.1 Household assets below nisab? Y/N. 2.2 Receiving zakat from another distributing body this period? Y/N. 2.3 Screener signature and date.

evidence.claim: The narrative describes funding a school year for children drawn from means-tested poor households, consistent with support to the poor and needy.
evidence.quote: Jamuna Learning Trust is funding a full academic year for 620 children from 410 families across fourteen schools in Tahirpur, Bishwamvarpur and Dowarabazar upazilas.

evidence.claim: The narrative describes cash stipends to the poorest households to offset lost child income, which is direct support to needy families.
evidence.quote: and for the poorest 140 households we pay a monthly stipend so the family is not choosing between a child's schooling and the income that child could bring in from fishing or day labour.

evidence.claim: The registered charitable purpose leads with advancing education rather than poverty relief, so the activity is partly an education programme rather than purely relief of the poor.
evidence.quote: Charitable purpose: Advancing education; relieving poverty, distress or disadvantage of individuals or families.

evidence.claim: Funds are paid per named pupil rather than as a block grant to the schools.
evidence.quote: The money does not go to the schools as a block grant. Fees are paid per pupil, against a named-pupil ledger that the school countersigns each term, and a copy of that ledger comes to us and to the family.

evidence.claim: The named-pupil ledger records individual pupils, amounts and dates, evidencing per-individual disbursement.
evidence.quote: Pupil ref TAH-0112, class 7, school D — fees BDT 4,200 paid 12 January, school countersign present, attendance 91%.

evidence.claim: Stipends are paid directly to a named household member by mobile money rather than to an institution.
evidence.quote: BDT 850 per month for twelve months to the 140 lowest-income households, paid by bKash to the mother where there is one in the household.

evidence.claim: Part of the appeal funds the organisation's own head office overhead rather than reaching individual households.
evidence.quote:
5. Head office rent and utilities — USD 3,800
   Share of our Melbourne office attributable to this appeal. Classified as administrative cost.

evidence.claim: The organisation concedes that on a stricter classification its non-beneficiary share of the appeal would be 12.8% rather than 6%.
evidence.quote: We note that a stricter reading would treat line 4 as administrative, which would put the figure at 12.8%.

evidence.claim: Household selection runs through a means test administered in the family's home.
evidence.quote: Household selection uses our means test, applied at the family's home rather than at the school.

evidence.claim: The means test has stated quantitative income, land and schooling thresholds.
evidence.quote: To qualify a household must report monthly income below BDT 11,000, must be landless or hold under 0.2 acres of homestead land, and must have a school-aged child either withdrawn from school in the previous eighteen months or at risk of withdrawal on the school's own register.

evidence.claim: The written intake instrument records income, land holding and a field officer signature with GPS point of visit.
evidence.quote:
1.1 Monthly household income, all sources, BDT. Threshold: below BDT 11,000.
1.2 Land: homestead acres owned, agricultural acres owned or sharecropped. Threshold: landless or under 0.2 acres homestead.

evidence.claim: Continuing need is re-verified twice a year at every enrolled household with recorded outcomes.
evidence.quote: Visit outcome recorded as continue / suspend / investigate. Round 1 of 2026: 410 households visited, 396 continue, 9 suspend, 5 investigate.

evidence.claim: The narrative states the stipends and fee payments are grants with no repayment by the family.
evidence.quote: The stipends and fee payments are grants and no family repays anything.

evidence.claim: Unused fees can be clawed back and reallocated when a child leaves, though the recovery is from the school rather than the household.
evidence.quote: If a child transfers or drops out, the remaining fees for that child are recovered from the school and reallocated, and this happened for nineteen children last year.

inferredCategoryReasoning: The substance is per-household support — school fees, uniforms and monthly cash stipends — reaching families selected against an income, land and vulnerability means test in rural Sunamganj, which is direct support to individuals below a locally-assessed sufficiency threshold. It is not fi_sabilillah because Bangladesh is not a region where Muslims are a minority.
